headline: Oil-price spike lifts revenue but derivatives hit profit
summary_short: Chord Energy's Q1 2026 revenue rose to $1.67B (+37.1% y/y) as crude prices spiked, but net income fell to $108.6M (-50.6% y/y) on a $241.5M derivative mark-to-market loss.
summary_long: Revenue rose to $1.67B, up 37.1% y/y and 42% q/q, as NYMEX WTI jumped over 50% after Middle East conflict escalation lifted realized crude prices ($70.05/bbl) and volumes, plus pass-through purchased-gas sales. Net income fell to $108.6M (-50.6% y/y) mainly on a $241.5M net loss on commodity derivatives from a shift in the futures curve; results also include a one-time $41.8M tax benefit tied to a prior tax-provision correction, pushing the effective tax rate to -15.2%. Operating cash flow was $507.5M (-22.8% y/y) on a working-capital drawdown. Chord paid a $1.30/share dividend, repurchased $70.7M of stock, and held $225.8M cash against $1.48B long-term debt. No production or capex guidance was given in this filing.

drivers.explanation: Highlights: Q1 production averaged 275,615 Boe/d (57% oil); NYMEX WTI rose over 50% after Middle East conflict escalation in late February, lifting realized prices; Chord paid a $1.30/share dividend and repurchased $70.7M of stock.
Crude oil revenue rose on higher realized prices and volumes sold; purchased oil-and-gas sales, which move with volumes purchased and resold, also grew sharply on higher crude volumes and prices.

Nearly flat y/y as revenue growth from higher crude prices was largely offset by a matching rise in purchased-oil-and-gas expense, which tracks the same pass-through volumes, plus higher DD&A and production taxes.

Fell y/y mainly on a $241.5M net loss on commodity derivatives from an upward shift in the crude-oil futures curve, versus a $20.3M loss a year earlier; a one-time $41.8M tax benefit partly offset this.
The y/y jump is a low-base effect: cash was drawn to $35.8M in Q1 2025 during the 2026 Senior Notes redemption and Credit Facility paydown; no comparable cash use recurred this quarter.
Debt roughly doubled y/y after the March 2025 issuance of $750M of 2033 Senior Notes, used to redeem the $400M 2026 Senior Notes and repay Credit Facility borrowings.
